newsitem.title: USA: American Image, Global Financial face new lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: American Image, Global Financial face new lawsuit.

text.p: American Image Motor Co Inc. and Global Financial Traders Ltd., an investment newsletter publisher, face yet another lawsuit alleging they manipulated the price of the motorcyle maker's stock, a plaintiff's lawyer said Thursday.
The class action suit, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, follows a civil complaint filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 14.
The lawsuits allege that Global's principals recommended that newsletter subscribers buy American Image's stock without telling them they held about 46 percent of the company's unrestricted stock.
The lawyer, Thomas Romans, represents plaintiff Peter Ellison, who filed the suit on behalf of shareholders who bought American Image stock between Sept. 23, 1996 and March 13, 1997.
The Santa Cruz, Calif.-based company's stock began trading on the Nasdaq bulletin board in August 1996.

The SEC's suit charges that the stock manipulation cost investors more than $1.5 million. It said American Image is purportedly a manufacturer of high-end motorcycles designed to compete with those made by Harley-Davidson Inc.
American Image was not available for comment.
